core_obligations: Identify the fibres as connected: the scheme theoretic fibres of the projection p : X x_k Y -> Y are base changes of the geometrically connected scheme X along field extensions, hence connected (proof lines 744-746).

Put the fibres in a usable form and check openness: the scheme theoretic fibres are homeomorphic to the set theoretic fibres, and the projection is an open map because a morphism of schemes over a field is universally open (proof lines 746-751).

Apply the topological criterion: with connected fibres and an open projection, the criterion on connected fibres and connected components applies and yields the asserted bijection between connected components (proof lines 752-754).
proof_roadmap: Observe that the fibres of the projection are base changes of the geometrically connected factor, hence connected (proof lines 744-746).
Replace scheme theoretic by set theoretic fibres and invoke universal openness over a field (proof lines 746-751).
Apply the standard topological criterion to conclude the bijection on connected components (proof lines 752-754).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if X is geometrically connected over k then the projection X x_k Y -> Y induces a bijection between connected components (statement lines 733-740). The proof assembles three separate facts about the projection: that its fibres are connected, because they are base changes of a geometrically connected scheme along field extensions; that the scheme theoretic fibres may be replaced by set theoretic ones; and that the map is open, which follows from a general result on morphisms of schemes over a field (proof lines 744-751). Only then does the topological criterion on connected fibres apply. The claim is H2: no construction, but a correct order of three cited inputs, and the openness step is the one that would be missed by a reader thinking only about fibres.
